headline: Harmonized metadata and uniform reprocessing make public sequencing archives reusable
label: Public Omics Metadata Harmonization
summary: New tools harmonize SRA, BioProject and GEO metadata as NCBI, CNCB-NGDC and PANTHER release 2027 updates to core archives and annotation resources.
synthesis: The dominant thread is converting raw public archives into findable, comparably processed data. SRAscout harmonizes SRA run and BioProject metadata for ~714,000 projects and adds BioBERT-embedding semantic search with filtering. MetaHQ integrates standardized annotations from 13 curation sources over 567k GEO samples and 27k studies, exposed through a Python CLI. Meta2Data automates retrieval, standardization and DADA2/VSEARCH processing of microbiome data across INSDC and CNCB. The Biodiversity Cell Atlas applies the same logic to single-cell data, uniformly reprocessing 39 whole-organism atlases from 33 eukaryotes behind a REST API. Underneath, the 2027 updates describe archive-level infrastructure: NCBI's SRA, GenBank and RefSeq with Submission Portal, NCBI Datasets and BLAST/annotation changes; CNCB-NGDC's thirteen new resources; and PANTHER's revised families, 131 genomes and expanded GO coverage. The extended tRNAdb compilation is a peripheral curated-reference update. New here is semantic, embedding-based discovery layered on harmonized metadata, alongside cross-archive (INSDC/CNCB) processing.
